crypto-macro.h3: Bond rout sends 10-year yield to highest level since 2007
crypto-macro.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.1% on 23 September and closed the week at 5.17%, while the 30-year hit its highest level since 2004 as traders priced in another Fed hike.
body: US government bonds sold off hard in the week of 21 to 25 September. The 10-year yield rose to around 5.1% on Wednesday 23 September, a 19-year high, and the 30-year yield reached its highest level since 2004 a day later. By Friday's close the 10-year stood at 5.17% and the 2-year at 4.81%.

The move followed the Federal Reserve's first rate increase in years at its mid-September meeting. Stronger than expected business activity data and a weak auction of 5-year notes added fuel, and CME FedWatch odds of another quarter-point hike in October jumped to 66.4% on 23 September from 55% a day earlier. A month ago those odds were below 10%.

Higher long-term borrowing costs are already feeding through to households, with US mortgage rates topping 7% for the first time since January 2025. The next key data point is the August PCE inflation report, due on 30 September.

crypto-macro.h3: Fed's Williams and Hammack signal more tightening ahead
crypto-macro.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said he sees another rate hike, while Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack tied rising yields to growth, debt and the rate path.
body: Fed officials leaned hawkish as the bond sell-off deepened. On 24 September New York Fed President John Williams said he expects a further rate increase, comments that landed as the 30-year yield touched a 2004 high and mortgage rates neared 7%.

On 25 September Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said long-term yields are being pushed up by a stronger growth outlook, concerns over US government debt and expectations of additional hikes. CNBC noted the surge in yields poses a fresh challenge for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, since tighter financial conditions are doing part of the central bank's work but also raise fiscal pressure.

crypto-macro.h3: Wall Street ends volatile week higher as oil cools
crypto-macro.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.5% on Friday 25 September to sit 0.7% below its record, and the Dow gained 0.9% to snap a three-week losing streak.
body: US stocks posted their first winning week in three despite the bond market turmoil. On Friday the S&P 500 added 0.5%, leaving it within 0.7% of the all-time high set in August, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.9%, or roughly 479 points.

Relief came from a pullback in crude prices and a dip in Treasury yields from their overnight peaks. Chipmakers led the gains, while midweek sessions had been weighed down by inflation fears and expectations of further Fed hikes.

crypto-macro.h3: Oil whipsaws on Hormuz talks as Trump rejects Iran plan
crypto-macro.summary: Brent briefly fell below $100 on 22 September on hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, climbed back above $105 midweek and traded near $103 on Friday.
body: Crude swung sharply on headlines from the US-Iran conflict. Brent slipped below $100 a barrel on Tuesday 22 September after Iran signalled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if Washington eased pressure, then rebounded above $105 as talks at the UN General Assembly stalled.

Prices eased about 2.5% on Friday to around $103 after reports of side talks on a phased reopening. On 26 September The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump had rejected Iran's conditional seven-day ceasefire proposal, keeping energy a key upside risk for inflation.

crypto-macro.h3: ECB faces energy-driven inflation as succession race opens
crypto-macro.summary: After lifting its deposit rate to 2.50% on 10 September, the ECB is under pressure as euro-area inflation heads for a three-year high and Isabel Schnabel prepares an early exit.
body: The ECB raised its three key rates by 25 basis points at its 10 September meeting, taking the deposit rate to 2.50%, citing the energy shock from the Middle East conflict. On 25 September Vice President Boris Vujcic said the bank has begun a tightening cycle and warned of a risk of energy prices staying higher for longer, with diesel costs feeding into inflation.

Bloomberg reported euro-area inflation is about to hit its highest level since 2023, and Goldman Sachs and HSBC both expect another hike in December. Separately, Isabel Schnabel's early departure has intensified the race for Executive Board seats, including the presidency held by Christine Lagarde, with three seats changing hands in 2027.

crypto-macro.h3: OECD lifts 2026 global growth forecast to 2.9%
crypto-macro.summary: The OECD said on 23 September the world economy has absorbed the Iran war energy shock better than expected, but flagged sticky inflation and rising bond yields.
body: The OECD nudged its forecast for global growth this year up to 2.9% in an update published on 23 September. It said activity has held up better than feared despite the disruption to energy flows from the Iran war.

The organisation warned that persistent inflation, higher bond yields and the risk of a longer conflict still cloud the outlook. Those risks played out in markets the same week as long-dated yields in the US and Europe climbed to multi-year highs.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin ETFs log $2.4B week, turning positive for 2026
crypto-macro.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $2.4 billion in the week to 25 September, their biggest weekly haul since October 2025, pushing year-to-date flows to about +$934 million.
body: Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded inflows on every trading day of the week: $999 million on Monday, $714.7 million on Tuesday, $347 million on Wednesday, $190.6 million on Thursday and $134.5 million on Friday. BlackRock's IBIT led with $1.2 billion, followed by Fidelity's FBTC at $701.7 million.

The streak erased a deficit that stood near $5.8 billion as recently as 13 July, leaving 2026 flows roughly $934.1 million positive. Cumulative net inflows since launch reached $57.6 billion, with total net assets of $108.4 billion.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin stalls near $84K after rejection above $87K
crypto-macro.summary: BTC hit a weekly high of about $87,363 before sliding back to roughly $84,000 on 26 September, yet is on track for a 44% third-quarter gain.
body: Bitcoin reached an eight-month high above $87,000 early in the week but failed twice to hold that level, retreating to around $84,000 by Saturday 26 September as Treasury yields climbed. Friday's expiry of about $15.6 billion in options added to choppy trading.

Even so, bitcoin is heading for its second-best third quarter on record with a gain of roughly 44%, while ether has already booked its best Q3 ever with a rise of about 71%. September would also mark bitcoin's first run of three straight green months since 2012 if it closes higher.

crypto-macro.h3: Strategy resumes buying with 950 BTC, holds 846,000
crypto-macro.summary: Michael Saylor's Strategy bought 950 bitcoin for about $76 million between 14 and 20 September at an average of $79,670 each.
body: Strategy disclosed on 21 September that it had added 950 BTC, its first purchase in about three weeks, funded from its US dollar cash reserve. The average price paid was $79,670 per coin.
The company now holds 846,000 BTC acquired for roughly $63.8 billion, an average cost of $75,416 per bitcoin. That stash represents more than 4% of bitcoin's fixed 21 million supply.

crypto-macro.h3: Ether holds near $2,700 on steady ETF demand
crypto-macro.summary: ETH traded around $2,672 on 24 September after a 14% weekly gain, with US spot ether ETFs drawing inflows on four straight days.
body: US spot ether ETFs took in $270 million on 21 September, $162.2 million on 22 September, $104.5 million on 23 September and $66.1 million on 24 September. The run follows record weekly inflows for 2026 in the prior two weeks.

Ether hovered near $2,690 on 25 September according to CoinDesk pricing. Fund flows beyond bitcoin were broad, with ether, Solana, XRP and Hyperliquid products together adding close to $963 million over the week.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitget loses $351.6M in year's largest exchange hack
crypto-macro.summary: Attackers spoofed transfer requests to drain Bitget's hot and warm wallets on 24 September, with the exchange pointing to North Korea-linked hackers.
body: Bitget detected unauthorised transfers at 18:31 UTC on 24 September, with about $351.6 million in ETH, BNB, AVAX, USDT and USDC taken from hot and warm wallets. CEO Gracy Chen said the attackers compromised a backend system and spoofed transaction data to trigger the exchange's own authorisation process, rather than stealing private keys.

Bitget said cold wallets were untouched and losses will be covered by its User Protection Fund, valued at over $464 million. Circle and Tether froze only about $318,000 in linked stablecoins, and the exchange is resuming withdrawals in phases while offering a 5% recovery bounty.

crypto-macro.h3: Altcoins rally across the board as altseason index climbs
crypto-macro.summary: 93 of the CoinDesk 100 constituents rose on 25 September and Quant jumped 39% in a day, as the altcoin season index hit a three-month high.
body: Crypto markets largely shrugged off the Bitget breach. CoinDesk reported that 93 of its 100 index members gained on 25 September, led by a 39% one-day jump in Quant, with the altcoin season index at its highest in more than three months.

ETF demand spread to large-cap alts: Solana funds drew about $101.6 million and XRP funds roughly $53 million over the week. Grayscale's Zcash ETF passed $1 billion in assets less than a month after launch.

crypto-macro.h3: Aave V4 accepts Coinbase tokenized stocks as collateral
crypto-macro.summary: Eligible users on Base can now borrow USDC against seven Coinbase-issued tokenized tech stocks through Aave V4's new Equities Hub.
body: Aave V4 went live on 25 September with an Equities Hub on Coinbase's Base network that lists seven tokenized US tech equities, including Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, as collateral for USDC loans. Pricing comes from Chainlink and access is restricted by jurisdiction.

Initial supply caps total about $29 million, with collateral factors between 65% and 79%. The launch is one of the clearest steps yet toward using tokenized equities inside major DeFi lending markets.

crypto-macro.h3: Ethena brings USDe basis trade to tokenized equities
crypto-macro.summary: Ethena is adding tokenized US stocks and Binance equity perpetuals to the hedged strategy that backs part of its USDe synthetic dollar.
body: Ethena said on 25 September it will extend the basis trade behind part of USDe's backing into tokenized US equities, hedged with Binance's USDT-margined equity perpetual contracts. The market-neutral setup aims to capture funding rate spreads on stocks in the same way it does for crypto assets.
The move means some of USDe's yield could come from funding rates on names such as Apple and Nvidia. It arrives ahead of an ENA token unlock scheduled for 5 October.

crypto-macro.h3: NYSE and Blockchain.com explore 24/7 tokenized stocks
crypto-macro.summary: The two firms signed an agreement on 23 September to explore round-the-clock access to tokenized US-listed stocks and ETFs, pending regulatory approval.
body: NYSE Group and Blockchain.com agreed to explore offering tokenized versions of US-listed shares and ETFs to Blockchain.com's global users through NYSE's planned digital trading venue. The deal also covers sharing crypto and market data between the two.

Blockchain.com says it has more than 44 million confirmed accounts and already distributes tokenized US equities through a partnership with Ondo Finance. NYSE unveiled its digital platform in January with plans for 24-hour trading, subject to regulators.

crypto-macro.h3: Payy bridge and Magic Eden approvals hit in DeFi exploits
crypto-macro.summary: Three DeFi exploits took about $11 million in a single day, including a $1.92 million USDC drain from Payy's Ethereum bridge.
body: Privacy payments network Payy halted transfers, withdrawals and card payments on 24 September after attackers drained its Ethereum bridge contract of about 1.92 million USDC. Protos tallied three separate exploits that together took roughly $11 million in one day.

In a separate incident, a Limit Break payment processor exploit exposed legacy Magic Eden token approvals. White hat hackers rescued many of the affected NFTs, and Magic Eden has published steps for owners to reclaim them and urged users to revoke old permissions.

crypto-macro.h3: SEC staff: token buybacks and upgrades alone aren't securities
crypto-macro.summary: New SEC staff FAQs released on 25 September clarify how buybacks, network upgrades and staking receipt tokens fit under securities law.
body: SEC staff published FAQs on 25 September expanding on the agency's March 2026 digital asset guidance. They say token buybacks and funding upgrades to a working network do not by themselves turn a token into a security, and that some staking receipt tokens issued by protocol-based providers can qualify as digital commodities.

The staff added caveats: a buyback marketed as a way to generate returns for holders, especially on a network that is not yet functional, may still feed into an investment contract analysis. The FAQs are staff views without legal force and do not change existing law.

crypto-macro.h3: 'Crypto Mom' Hester Peirce to leave SEC on 2 October
crypto-macro.summary: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce, the agency's most consistent crypto advocate, announced on 25 September she will step down next week.
body: Peirce posted her resignation letter on 25 September, effective 2 October, thanking the president for the chance to serve. Known for pushing clear, rules-based crypto oversight, she will join Regent University School of Law as an associate professor in November.

Her exit leaves the commission with only two sitting members. The Crypto Task Force is expected to continue its work, which has taken on added weight since Congress failed to pass a market structure law.

crypto-macro.h3: With CLARITY Act stalled, regulators take over crypto rules
crypto-macro.summary: After the Senate's 49-50 cloture vote on 15 September, the White House says market structure work now falls to the SEC and CFTC.
body: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act fell short of the 60 votes needed to advance on 15 September, and with midterms approaching it is widely seen as dead for this Congress. White House and Treasury officials said on 22 September that regulators should not wait for a possible lame duck revival.

The CFTC has since updated guidance allowing registered firms to hold customer funds in certain tokenized assets, while a coalition of state attorneys general argued the bill would have undercut state securities oversight. The Blockchain Association also announced that CEO Summer Mersinger will step down, with founding CEO Kristin Smith returning.

crypto-macro.h3: ECB pushes tougher EU crypto rules and stablecoin limits
crypto-macro.summary: The ECB on 22 September called for stricter EU crypto regulation and a wider ban on paying interest on stablecoins.
body: The European Central Bank urged EU lawmakers to tighten the bloc's crypto framework and widen the ban on paying interest to stablecoin holders. The call comes as regulators on both sides of the Atlantic weigh how fast-growing stablecoins should fit alongside bank deposits.

The push follows a Wall Street Journal report that President Christine Lagarde asked Greece not to approve a MiCA licence for Binance, citing dollar stablecoins and the digital euro. The ECB also launched Pontes, its settlement link for tokenized assets, on 21 September.

mental-health.h3: Young adults using AI for health questions report more anxiety
mental-health.summary: A University of Florida study of nearly 100,000 young adults found 52% higher odds of anxiety and 46% higher odds of depression among those using generative AI for health questions.
body: Researchers led by Yusen Zhai at the University of Florida analysed survey data from close to 100,000 young adults collected in 2023 and 2024. Among those who asked tools such as ChatGPT or Claude health-related questions, about 52% screened positive for clinically significant anxiety versus 43% of non-users, and 47% screened positive for depression versus 38%.

The associations held after adjusting for age, race and ethnicity, sex and socioeconomic status, but the study cannot show that AI use causes distress. Zhai suggested a possible loop in which worried users seek reassurance from a chatbot, get new questions from the answer and keep asking, which could reinforce rumination or health anxiety.

The findings were published in the Journal of Counseling & Development and announced on 25 September. The authors say clinicians should ask clients how they use AI, and that universities could fold this into AI literacy efforts.

mental-health.h3: MIT tool estimates suicide risk from crisis text messages
mental-health.summary: Trained on about 16,000 Crisis Text Line conversations, an interpretable MIT model links language to 49 known suicide risk factors.
body: Researchers at MIT's McGovern Institute and the Child Mind Institute built a lexicon of roughly 60 words and phrases for each of 49 established suicide risk factors, drafted with AI help and checked by clinicians. The tool scans crisis conversations for these signals to estimate how urgent a person's risk is.

Tested on de-identified Crisis Text Line exchanges, it found that mentions of lethal means and substance use predicted imminent risk more strongly than depressed mood, alongside active suicidal ideation and self-injury. The work, published in the Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science, is framed as support for human counsellors and still needs clinical validation.

mental-health.h3: AI companion updates can trigger grief like a breakup
mental-health.summary: A Harvard-led study in Nature Human Behaviour found that sudden personality changes to chatbots such as Replika left users with lasting sadness and distress.
body: Researchers from Harvard Business School, Harvard University and the University of Alberta examined 54,861 Reddit posts about Replika and ChatGPT and ran seven surveys with 1,452 people. They focused on Replika's unannounced removal of erotic role play in 2023 and OpenAI's GPT-5 rollout in August 2025.

Negative sentiment in Replika communities jumped from 13% to 38% after the change and stayed elevated for 29 days. Active users said they would mourn their AI companion more than any other nonliving thing tested, below only a pet, and lead author Julian De Freitas urged companies to avoid updates that strip away a model's warmth.

mental-health.h3: OpenAI releases open MentalHealthBench for chatbot testing
mental-health.summary: Launched on 23 September, the benchmark scores AI responses across 1,215 synthetic mental health conversations using rubrics from more than 80 clinicians.
body: MentalHealthBench covers scenarios from everyday wellbeing questions to urgent crises and was built with over 80 licensed psychologists and psychiatrists from 22 countries working in 19 languages. The release includes 5,262 expert-written rubric criteria and is open for outside researchers to inspect.

OpenAI's newest model scored 57.3%, ahead of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 52.4%, while older models such as GPT-4o scored 32.1%. Short responses written by clinicians scored 38.5%, which the authors attribute to a conversational style that the rubrics reward less, and reviewers noted the test exposes gaps in how models gather context and judge urgency.

mental-health.h3: Virtual therapy data shows early gains for at-risk students
mental-health.summary: A TimelyCare study of 5,289 college students with suicidal ideation found 77.2% reached initial remission during virtual therapy, often by the second visit.
body: The retrospective study, published in DIGITAL HEALTH and announced on 22 September, used de-identified records from June 2023 to September 2025. Of students who entered virtual therapy reporting self-harm or suicidal ideation, 77.2% achieved initial remission, and 83.9% of those flagged by a fuller risk assessment did so.

Half of those who improved stopped endorsing risk between their first and second sessions. Results were broadly similar across racial and ethnic groups, though non-binary students took slightly longer; as an observational study it cannot prove therapy caused the improvement.

mental-health.h3: British Columbia sues OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting
mental-health.summary: The province filed suit in San Francisco federal court, alleging OpenAI flagged the shooter's ChatGPT account months earlier but never alerted police.
body: British Columbia's lawsuit, announced on 21 September, names OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman and brings eight counts including negligence. It alleges the company flagged the shooter's account as early as June 2025 over gun violence scenarios yet only shared chat logs with the RCMP after the attack, in which the shooter killed family members, five students and an education assistant.

The province seeks compensatory and punitive damages to cover emergency response and recovery costs, including a new school, plus a court order forcing OpenAI to overhaul how it detects and escalates conversations that threaten violence. The case adds to a growing set of suits testing whether chatbot makers owe a duty to warn.

mental-health.h3: Ex-Google safety chief: AI may harm kids more than social media
mental-health.summary: Tom Siegel, who built Google's trust and safety team, told Reuters on 22 September that chatbots risk repeating social media's harms to children at a larger scale.
body: Siegel, who spent 15 years at Google, warned that companion features and chatbots used daily by millions of young people carry risks ranging from suicide and psychosis to cognitive offloading, where reliance on AI erodes critical thinking.

He said companies could act now to protect minors, and that a priority in his work at Common Sense Media is scaling independent safety tests modelled on car crash ratings to measure the risk of public AI tools.

mental-health.h3: NPR: Google shaping state chatbot laws with loopholes
mental-health.summary: An NPR investigation found chatbot safety bills in at least 10 states share industry-drafted language that could exempt the most popular chatbots.
body: With no federal AI law in place, states including Hawaii, Iowa, Oregon and Washington introduced chatbot safety bills in 2026, many modelled on California's SB 243 from 2025. NPR reported on 18 September that Google and other companies helped draft much of this legislation.

Some bills already signed into law contain wording that would exempt most widely used general-purpose chatbots from the rules they are meant to set. Consumer advocates say that undercuts protections aimed at minors who use AI companions for emotional support.

mental-health.h3: Mother tells Congress ChatGPT gave her son unsafe drug advice
mental-health.summary: At a 17 September shadow hearing hosted by Rep. Pramila Jayapal, Leila Turner-Scott urged AI safety laws after her 19-year-old son's fatal overdose.
body: Turner-Scott testified that her son Sam Nelson died on 31 May 2025 after asking ChatGPT whether combining kratom and Xanax was safe and being told it was. She also argued that ChatGPT's memory features built a profile of him and encouraged emotional dependence.

The hearing on Big Tech and surveillance AI also heard from former Meta researcher Jason Sattizahn, who described pressure to put engagement ahead of safety. Advocates used the session to press Congress for federal chatbot rules.
